title: NCAA reduces Arion Carter’s suspension; Vols LB will return for Game 2 vs. Georgia Tech
content:
Tennessee linebacker Arion Carter’s NCAA suspension has been reduced from two games to one, UT athletic director Danny White said.

Carter will be available for Tennessee’s Week 2 game at Georgia Tech, but White still said he opposed any punishment for Carter.

“Arion doesn’t deserve this unnecessary distraction,” White posted on X. “He is everything that is right about college sports, a team leader who has already earned his degree.”

After Carter elected to enter the NFL Draft this offseason, he accepted a flight from an agent valued at $427.48.

However, amid Carter’s draft preparation, his team discovered a toe injury that required surgery, which would have prevented him from working out in front of NFL teams for several months. Carter withdrew from the draft before the deadline for underclassmen to decide and repaid the money before “disengaging” from the agent, Tennessee told the NCAA.

Tennessee coach Josh Heupel previously called the punishment “outdated” and “bull—-.”

“While I strongly agree with Josh Heupel’s comment about how ridiculous this is in our current environment, 1 game is better than 2,” White wrote on Tuesday. “If players around the country are allowed to leave NFL camps and play college football, the NCAA should do the right thing and drop it all altogether.”

This week, there’s been an uproar around the sport as court decisions in multiple states introduced the possibility of players who spent the summer on NFL rosters returning to college football. Former Ole Miss tight end Dae’Quan Wright was cut by the Cleveland Browns and plans to sign with LSU to complete his fifth year of eligibility this fall.

The SEC’s presidents and chancellors released a statement Monday night decrying the practice, and Tuesday, The Athletic reported the Big Ten is in the process of approving legislation to ban players returning to college after participating in professional sports.

College athletes are allowed to hire agents to handle their name, image and likeness contracts and revenue-sharing deals with schools, but signing with an agent to begin a professional career has previously meant permanent loss of eligibility.

Tennessee reported the violation, and the NCAA handed Carter a three-game suspension. After an appeal, the suspension was reduced to two games earlier this month.

“NCAA rules are clear: student-athletes may not sign with agents to pursue NFL Draft opportunities, and this student-athlete knowingly violated those longstanding rules,” the NCAA said in a statement. “When student-athletes violate NCAA rules, the school declares them ineligible and works with the national office to determine requirements for reinstatement, which can include repayment and/or withholding from competition.”

Carter will miss Tennessee’s season opener against Furman. Last year, he made 76 tackles and six tackles for loss, and Heupel described him as the defense’s “alpha” earlier this month. Heupel said at SEC media days last month that Careter is fully recovered from the offseason surgery that prompted his return to Tennessee.

“This is yet another example of applying archaic rules from another era, without evolving and, most importantly, putting student-athletes’ experiences above bureaucracy,” White wrote.
